name: Michal
title: Saul's daughter and David's first wife
summary: Michal was the daughter of King Saul and became David's first wife. She loved David and helped him escape her father's murder plots, but their relationship later became marked by bitterness. She is known for despising David when he danced before the ark of the covenant, which led to her remaining childless for the rest of her life.

keyEvents.title: Michal is given to David as a wife
keyEvents.description: Saul offered Michal to David as a wife in exchange for one hundred Philistine foreskins, hoping that David would be killed. David succeeded, and Michal became his wife.

keyEvents.title: Michal helps David escape
keyEvents.description: When Saul sent men to kill David, Michal helped him flee through a window and deceived the pursuers with a household idol placed in the bed.

keyEvents.title: Mikal is given to Paltiel
keyEvents.description: After David fled, Saul gave Mikal to Paltiel son of Lajish as a wife.

keyEvents.title: David demands the return of Mikal
keyEvents.description: When David became king over Judah, he demanded that Ish-bosheth give Mikal back to him. Paltiel followed her weeping but was sent away.

keyEvents.title: Mikal despises David for dancing before the ark
keyEvents.description: As David danced with joy before the ark of the covenant being brought into Jerusalem, Mikal looked down on him from the window and despised him in her heart.

keyEvents.title: Mikal remains childless
keyEvents.description: As a consequence of despising David, Mikal had no children until the day she died, which in biblical context was seen as God's judgment.
